source.title: Andriatsitohaina et al. (2020), Effects of habitat edges on vegetation structure and the vulnerable golden-brown mouse lemur (Microcebus ravelobensis) in northwestern Madagascar
source.version: BMC Ecology 20, article 69 (2020); version of record published 2020-12-17
source.locator: Abstract; Methods §§Study site and period, Data collection, and Data analyses; Results §§Effects of edge habitats on M. ravelobensis abundance and body mass, Relationship between edge effects in vegetation and M. ravelobensis abundance and body mass; Discussion; article license statement.
source.licenseAppliesTo: Article text used for paraphrased research findings. No figures, photographs, or separately credited third-party material are reused; the publisher notes that some third-party material may have separate credit-line terms.
source.scope: Primary field research on wild, free-ranging Microcebus ravelobensis sampled along four forest-edge transects in Mariarano Classified Forest, northwestern Madagascar, during 2017-2018. The measured responses are local capture-based abundance and body mass, not a species-wide range, population estimate, or diagnostic description.
source.attribution: Andriatsitohaina B, Romero-Mujalli D, Ramsay MS, Kiene F, Rasoloharijaona S, Rakotondravony R, Lehman SM, Radespiel U (2020). BMC Ecology 20, 69. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12898-020-00337-z. Claims paraphrased; no figures reused.

ecology.text: At Mariarano Classified Forest, four 1-km transects perpendicular to forest edges were sampled in 2017-2018 with 2,424 trap-nights, yielding 226 captured M. ravelobensis. A logistic model estimated a 340-m depth of edge influence for capture-based local abundance, but the overall edge-versus-interior abundance difference was not significant; the male-only difference was a statistical trend (p=0.082), and the female comparison was not significant (p=0.843). Within these transects, abundance was negatively associated with measured densities of large trees, small trees, and saplings. These results describe one local sample and do not establish a causal edge effect, total population size, or a species-wide pattern.
ecology.locator: Abstract; Methods §§Study site and period and Data collection (four transects, 2,424 trap-nights, and abundance as unique captures per 100 m); Results §Effects of edge habitats on M. ravelobensis abundance and body mass (DEI 340 m and nonsignificant overall comparison); Results §Relationship between edge effects in vegetation and M. ravelobensis abundance and body mass (Fig. 6a-c and Table S4); Discussion §Edge effects on M. ravelobensis.
ecology.placeTimeScope: Mariarano Classified Forest, near Mariarano village, about 80 km northeast of Mahajanga, northwestern Madagascar (15°24′S, 46°44′E; 20-90 m elevation). Transect C1 was sampled in June-July 2017; C2-C4 were sampled from mid-May to mid-August 2018. Four 1-km transects bordered different road, savannah, and agricultural matrices.
ecology.lifeStatus: Wild, free-ranging field captures. Captured animals were handled briefly and released at dusk at their capture locations; no captive, domesticated, or fossil population is represented.

morphology.text: In the same wild Mariarano sample, captured M. ravelobensis were weighed and age-classified; adults were defined using body mass of at least 41 g together with other morphometric parameters. A logistic model estimated a 390-m depth of edge influence for local body-mass variation, but the overall edge-versus-interior body-mass difference was not significant; the female-only contrast was a statistical trend (p=0.052), with no corresponding male trend. This local response does not establish a species-wide body-mass range, diagnostic morphology, or sexual dimorphism.
morphology.locator: Methods §Data collection (individual weighing and adult classification); Results §Effects of edge habitats on M. ravelobensis abundance and body mass (DEI 390 m and nonsignificant overall comparison); Fig. 5b and Table S3 (female-only p=0.052 trend); Discussion §Edge effects on M. ravelobensis.
morphology.placeTimeScope: Wild captured animals at Mariarano Classified Forest, northwestern Madagascar, sampled on four 1-km forest-edge transects in June-July 2017 and mid-May-mid-August 2018. The paper reports a local modeled response and does not estimate a range-wide body-mass distribution.
morphology.lifeStatus: Wild, free-ranging field captures. The study did not measure captive, domesticated, or fossil animals.

ecology: The evidence is limited to one forest and four transects with different matrix types. Overall edge-interior abundance differences were nonsignificant, and the authors discuss the small transect sample and moderate, spatially variable responses.

Trap captures per 100 m are a local abundance index, not an estimate of population density or total population size. Vegetation associations are observational and do not establish causal effects or a general species-wide response.
morphology: Only body mass and an adult-classification threshold are reported for a local wild sample. The study does not establish a species-wide body-mass range, diagnostic morphology, ontogenetic pattern, or sexual dimorphism; overall edge-interior body-mass differences were nonsignificant.

identityScope: The target is the exact accepted COL26.8 usage 42SBZ. The paper studies individuals identified as Microcebus ravelobensis at one northwestern Madagascar forest site; it does not define or compare subspecies, so none is inferred.
wildScope: The cited biological data are from wild mouse lemurs captured at Mariarano Classified Forest on four 1-km transects in 2017-2018. Animals were briefly handled, weighed, and released at dusk at their capture sites. No captive, domesticated, or fossil evidence is included.
completenessReasons: One primary field study supports only local ecology and body-mass response; it does not establish range-wide species patterns.
Life history, evolution, distribution, fossil evidence, and current conservation status remain unassessed.
No comprehensive multi-source review or independent expert review has been completed.
